title: Batch Oracle: workload-signature heuristics and gradual apply for continuous batching recommendations
creator: Priya Singh
description: Build ‘Batch Oracle’, a continuous recommendation engine that profiles per-workload request signatures, applies rule-based and ML-derived heuristics to propose batching and caching parameters, and performs a graduated safe-apply/rollback with observability hooks. The aim is to cut per-token unit cost while preserving tail-latency SLOs and quality regressions across hosted and dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Profile collector captures workload signatures (seq_len_distribution, prompt_prefix_fingerprints, kv_cache_hitrate, concurrency_profiles) for 95% of production routes without adding >1% tail latency.
Recommendation engine outputs deterministic proposals: batch_size_target, max_queue_ms, kv_cache_policy, kv_prefix_eviction for each workload cohort and stores proposal metadata for auditing.
Safe-apply flow: shadow-apply -> canary (1%) -> ramp (5%, 25%, 100%) with automated rollback triggers on cost/latency/quality thresholds and optional manual approval at canary stage.
Rollback criteria include: p99 latency increase > 15% vs baseline, token-cost reduction < 5% with latency regression, or model quality regression detected by eval prompts.
End-to-end telemetry surfaced in Console: per-route recommendation diff, estimated cost impact, canary metrics, and root-cause links to traces/PRs.
Playbook and runbook added to Confluence with step-by-step safe-apply and manual override instructions and at least two runbook-led simulated rollbacks completed in staging.
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, telemetry, and product. Agreed on workload signature schema and privacy constraints (strip PII, only hashed prompt prefixes).
2026-02-18: Prototype collector implemented in shadow mode for 10 routes; verified <0.5% median extra latency using async sampling. Collector PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1426

2026-02-26: Heuristics spec drafted - includes latency-sensitive guardrails, kv-hint rules (prefer prefix-caching for stable routing keys), and coalescence thresholds based on inter-arrival-time percentiles. Confluence doc: drive.redwood.com/BatchOracle/spec-v1

2026-03-04: End-to-end simulator (stressor) built to replay route traffic with proposed batch configs; observed cost reductions of 9-16% on synthetic cohorts but p99 spikes on renegade microburst workload patterns. Added microsmoothing to proposal generation.

2026-03-09: Implemented safe-apply pipeline in CI: shadow-apply artifacts are validated, canary rollout automation created. Playbook draft ready for review by SRE and PM. PR for rollout engine: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2783
2026-03-12: Internal review with Product and SRE. Action items: add ML-backed anomaly detector for quality regressions, incorporate per-tenant opt-out, and expose manual hold at 5% ramp.
decisions: Use mixed heuristic + lightweight ML ranking: heuristics generate candidate params, a small XGBoost-style model ranks candidates by expected cost/latency tradeoff. Rationale: deterministic, explainable suggestions and low runtime footprint.
Telemetry collection will only retain aggregated signatures and hashed prompt fingerprints for 90 days by default to address privacy/compliance concerns.
Default safe-apply sequence: shadow -> canary 1% (24h) -> staged ramp 5% (12h) -> 25% (6h) -> 100% with automated rollback thresholds. Manual approval gate before 25% for routes flagged high-risk.
Aggressive batching disabled for routes with kv_cache_hitrate < 10% or p95 short-tail latency sensitivity tag.
tradeoffs: Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases queuing latency for cold requests and can worsen p99 when microbursts occur. We prioritize SLO preservation over marginal cost wins for high-value routes.
Keeping heuristics interpretable limits the complexity of the model; we avoid deep black-box models that would be harder to audit during rollbacks.
Shadow collection adds telemetry overhead; to minimize impact we sample at route-level with adaptive sampling and limit per-route retention.
